transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I’m here because I can’t seem to sit still much anymore. For the past year or so I’m always puttering around—fixing things, arranging things, saying yes to one more volunteer thing. Even at my age, I have trouble just sitting down and being still.
During this time, have you been needing less sleep than usual?
I don’t think so… not that I’ve really noticed. I sleep about the same, as far as I can tell.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot?
Not especially, no. I mean… I worry about the usual things, I suppose, but I wouldn’t say it’s a lot.
During this period, have you been feeling unusually cheerful or high?
No… I wouldn’t say high or unusually cheerful. I’ve just been… myself, I suppose.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?
Not really… I mean, I forget little things sometimes, but nothing that feels unusual to me.
Do you get distracted easily?
I suppose sometimes, yes… if there’s a lot going on around me. But I haven’t really kept track of it.
Has this restlessness been causing problems in your daily life?
A little, yes. At the senior center, I’ve had to apologize after meetings… and one friend said maybe I should take a smaller role at the sign-up table, because I was making things a bit tense.
Have there been times when you felt much more irritable than usual?
I don’t know… I can get a bit short with people sometimes, I suppose. But much more than usual? I haven’t really noticed that.
Did you have this kind of trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Yes… I think so. I remember in grade school getting scolded for jumping up out of my seat, and talking over the other children. They used to say I was “too lively,” that sort of thing… this was before I was a teenager.
Do these periods of being unable to sit still come in clear episodes, or is it more or less always been that way for you?

It’s more… sort of always there, I think. Not really in clear spells. Like at the senior center meetings, or during church announcements, I get that ants-in-my-chair feeling and I’ll shift around or get up for coffee, straighten papers—just to get through it.
